description: meta ads must haves: episode 1 🎬 if you're brand new to meta ads, this is where you start. most people jump straight into running campaigns without actually understanding what they're doing or why it works. so i'm breaking down the fundamentals in this series so you know exactly what you're working with before you touch the platform. episode 1: the difference between paid social and paid search meta (facebook + instagram) is a PUSH platform. you're pushing your message out to brand new audiences based on their interests, behaviors, demographics — all the data meta has collected about them. google (search ads) is a PULL platform. people are actively searching for what you sell. you're pulling them in based on their search intent. either they're looking for your product directly, your industry, or a problem your product solves. why does this matter? because it changes your entire strategy. meta is for awareness and consideration. google is for when someone's already ready to buy. most e-commerce brands need BOTH. but meta is where the real money is for beginners because the audience is so much bigger. episode 2 drops soon and we're talking campaign structure! the three tier system that makes everything click. follow along so you don't miss it 👆

As long as you have Wi-Fi and a laptop, you can make a fuck ton of money, quit your 9 to 5, and work a fraction of the time, basically giving you total time, location, and financial freedom. I can vouch for this because this is what I do. So to kick off the series, I really just want to lay the groundwork of what exactly meta ads are. Meta ads are the advertisements that people see in their Facebook and Instagram feed. And these are served to people based on their interest, behaviors, demographic, or proximity to certain things. So the way that I like to think about it is when I think of digital advertising in general, I categorize it into two separate groups, right? We have paid social, and then we have paid search. Paid social is going to be social media platforms. Instagram, TikTok, Pinterest, YouTube. And then paid search is going to be essentially Google. So between these two, we have a push versus a pull method. Push means You are pushing your content out to brand new people, cold audiences. And that is exactly what paid social does. Right? So how many times have you been scrolling on Instagram and you came across a product that you have never heard of once in your life, and it solves the problem that you didn't even know existed? That is the power of paid social. And meta just so happens to be the biggest paid social platform. Whereas, on the contrary, Google is a pull platform.
